expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any observable series is expected. The duplicate-key signature should continue to be observable while the condition persists: SQLSTATE 23505 lines on order_pkey in accounting's logs and errored accounting/otel leaf spans under accounting/order-consumed in Tempo. The correct next step is investigative, not remediative — a direct read of the accounting Postgres order table and of the consumer group's committed offsets, neither of which this system is permitted to perform.
if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a dispatch against Postgres or the broker shows the order table was populated by a prior workload and the new consumer is replaying from a stale offset — in which case the correct fix is restore_data (clear/reconcile the order table or advance the offset), which this executor cannot perform (restore_store is UNAVAILABLE, T6.2). It is also wrong if fresh metrics show the 23505 rate is already zero and the burst at 09:43:11–09:44:06 was self-limiting, in which case there is nothing to remediate at all. Note that the metrics here cannot settle this: the baseline window returned zero samples and three intervals had no traffic [tr_87ce6ad1d4f7], so neither onset nor current state is measurable, and an effect from any action would be largely unobservable.
risk: The risk being avoided is the risk of acting. restart_service is the only action whose preconditions are even arguably touched, and it is not met: the evidence points at the contents of accounting's datastore, not at process state — the consumer is alive and processing orders one second after each exception [tr_d652adf5048e], so there is no wedged process to recreate. Recreating the container would discard nothing that matters, would not change the rows already in the order table, and the same messages would be re-consumed and re-rejected with 23505 the moment the consumer rejoins — a change that looks like action, costs an availability gap, and fixes nothing. rollback_image and revert_config both fail their preconditions outright: the change log for the full 24 hours contains exactly one event, a first-time container creation, with no deploy, image bump, or config edit recorded [tr_079b4ae39041], so there is no prior image tag or prior configuration to return to. Proposing either would be an action against a change that did not happen. The named fix class, restore_data, is unavailable to this executor.
blast_radius: None from this proposal, since nothing is executed. For reference, had restart_service been proposed the blast radius would be accounting alone for the duration of the recreate, plus the orders its consumer would not drain during that window; the blast radius given names only accounting (seed, alerted) and no inbound callers, so no other service is recorded as observing it. The cost of abstaining is that duplicate-key rejections continue and some orders go unpersisted until someone with datastore access intervenes.
